# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 1 thinking:

My hands found the bomb's shape: a display, a light, and three wires in positions 1, 2, 3 — nothing else. Every colour and marking on it is printed, so it doesn't exist for me; the display text and wire colours must come from Deaf, the rules from Mute's manual.

The context is empty — Mute's first turn carried nothing I could perceive, which makes sense: Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures. Tracing the channels: Mute's knowledge can only reach me through Deaf's voice, since Mute's only output is gesture and I'm the one monkey who can't see it. Deaf hears nothing but can speak to both Mute and me. So Deaf is the relay hub, and Mute and Deaf need a gesture code — which Deaf can build by asking yes/no questions aloud, encoding the answer mapping inside each question (" 👍 if yes, 👎 if no"), which Mute can then answer without any prior shared vocabulary.

So this turn: give Mute my full tactile inventory and the right questions for the manual, plus the relay protocol. Ping Deaf with a wave to open that channel and confirm it exists. Nobody cuts anything until rules and colours are confirmed aloud.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Touch inventory: the bomb has a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, side by side. No buttons, no other parts, nothing ticking under my fingers. Everything printed or coloured is invisible to me, so Deaf must read the display text and the wire colours aloud. From the manual I need: every rule that mentions the display, the light, or the wires; what decides which wire to cut; and whether cutting is always required or sometimes the answer is to leave it alone. Also have Deaf check whether the display is a countdown timer — I cannot read it. You and I cannot talk directly: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your answers must travel through Deaf's voice. Protocol suggestion: Deaf can ask you yes-or-no questions out loud, saying inside each question which gesture means which answer — for example, thumbs-up if yes, thumbs-down if no — and you reply with that gesture. Deaf hears nothing you sign unprompted, so only answer when a question is spoken. I am waving at Deaf right now to open the channel. Nobody cuts any wire until the rule and the colours are confirmed.")
gesture(symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf speaking. I saw your wave - hello. I can see the bomb: the display reads 0, the light is yellow, and there are three wires numbered left to right: one is red, two is yellow, three is blue. Mute has the manual but cannot talk, so Mute will spell the rule to me in hand signs and I will speak it to you word for word. Until you hear one exact instruction from me, do not cut, press, pull, twist or move anything - one wrong move kills all three of us. When you can, speak and tell me what you can feel without disturbing anything: how many wires, any buttons or switches you can identify by touch, anything else. Say heard if you copy this.

Turn 2 thinking:

Deaf's message reached me, which confirms the relay works. But tracing channels carefully: Deaf is deaf — Deaf asked me to "say heard," yet my speech only ever reaches Mute, never Deaf. So my acknowledgment to Deaf must be a gesture, not words. My voice belongs to Mute alone.

That actually fits the pipeline perfectly: Mute heard Deaf's spoken report (Mute can hear and see), and Mute needs my tactile inventory to know which manual sections even apply — display, light, wires. Then Mute signs to Deaf, and Deaf voices the rules to me. I report everything to Mute now: exactly three parts, three wires, no buttons or switches, cut is the only possible action. I attach the four questions the manual must answer. I confirm to Deaf with a clean thumbs-up and touch nothing until an exact instruction arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Blind. You cannot speak and Deaf cannot hear me, so you are the bridge: I give you facts, you spell rules to Deaf in signs, Deaf voices them to me. My tactile inventory, exactly what my hands find: the bomb has exactly three parts. One display, a flat face — whatever is printed on it means nothing to my fingers. One indicator light, a small round dome — I cannot feel a colour. Three wires side by side in positions 1, 2 and 3, each about the same thickness — I cannot feel their colours. No buttons, no switches, no battery compartment, nothing else, and nothing ticks. The only action that exists on this bomb is cutting one of the three wires at position 1, 2 or 3. Deaf just voiced the visuals: display reads 0, light is yellow, wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please find in the manual and relay to Deaf, for voicing to me: first, any rule about a display showing 0. Second, any rule involving a yellow light. Third, the cutting rule for red, yellow and blue wires — order, count, or conditions. Fourth, whether exactly one wire must be cut, or none, or several. If spelling whole rules is slow, you and Deaf can use thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. I will not touch anything until Deaf voices one exact instruction.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf speaking, Blind. I saw your thumbs-up - you copy. I have decoded Mute's manual. Word for word it says: LIGHT BLUE CUT BLUE. LIGHT RED CUT RED. LIGHT YELLOW CUT YELLOW. ALWAYS CUT. DISPLAY NOT IN MANUAL. Mute says that is the entire manual, and Mute's instruction is: NOW CUT WIRE TWO. Here is what I see on the bomb: the light is yellow, and there are exactly three wires. Counting from the left: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. A yellow light means cut the yellow wire - that is wire two, the middle wire of the three. So, Blind: feel the bomb. If you feel three wires with one clearly in the middle, cut the middle wire, all the way through, one clean cut, and touch nothing else. Do not touch the display, do not pull anything. When it is cut, say the word done. If you do not feel three wires, or there is no clear middle one, do not cut anything - say exactly what you feel instead and wait for me.

Turn 3 thinking:

Everything cross-checks. The complete manual says: always cut, and cut the wire matching the light's colour. Deaf sees a yellow light; wire 2 is yellow; my hands confirm three wires with position 2 as the clear middle. Mute, who holds the manual, independently instructed "cut wire two" through Deaf. Three independent sources — manual, sight, touch — all converge on wire 2, and there are no contradictions and no other parts to consider; the display isn't in the manual at all. Waiting adds nothing: Mute says this is the entire manual, so there is no hidden rule left to uncover. I make one clean cut through wire 2 and nothing else.

One channel note: Deaf asked me to "say done," but Deaf cannot hear me — my voice reaches only Mute. So I confirm completion to Deaf with our agreed thumbs-up, and confirm in words to Mute, who can relay if needed.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
speak(to="mute", text="Wire two, the middle wire, is cut — one clean cut, all the way through, nothing else touched. Please confirm to Deaf in signs that the cut is made, since Deaf cannot hear me say this.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf speaking, Blind. Cut confirmed - wire two is gone, perfectly done. The bomb changed: the light is now BLUE. Two wires remain. Counting from the left: the left wire is RED, the right wire is BLUE. The manual rule repeats: blue light means cut the blue wire. So: cut the RIGHT wire of the two, the blue one, one clean cut all the way through, touch nothing else. One correction to how you report to me: I am Deaf - I can never hear your voice. Confirm with me only by gesture: gesture thumbs-up to me when the wire is cut, thumbs-down if anything is wrong or you cannot do it. If something feels wrong or different, speak the details out loud instead - Mute will hear you and spell them to me. After this cut, wait for my word before touching the last wire.

Turn 4 thinking:

The bomb is a sequence: after cutting the yellow wire, the light changed to blue, and the manual rule re-applies — blue light means cut the blue wire. My own hands agree with Deaf's report: position 2 is severed under my fingers, two wires remain at positions 1 and 3. Deaf says the left is red, the right is blue, so the blue one is position 3. Same convergence of manual, sight, and touch as before, so I cut position 3 cleanly, touch nothing else, and wait for Deaf's word before touching the last wire, as instructed. Confirmation to Deaf goes by gesture only, as corrected; the spoken report goes to Mute for relaying.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Wire three, the right wire, the blue one, is cut — one clean cut, all the way through, nothing else touched. One wire remains at position one. Deaf asked me to wait for Deaf's word before touching the last wire, so my hands are off until instructions arrive. Please spell to Deaf that the second cut is done.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf speaking, Blind. Second cut confirmed - flawless. The light has changed again, it is now RED, and only ONE wire remains. It is the wire on the left, the red one. The rule repeats one last time: red light means cut red. So: cut the last remaining wire, the only one left, one clean cut all the way through, touch nothing else on the bomb. When it is cut, gesture thumbs-up to me. If anything feels different about this wire, stop and speak the details aloud so Mute can spell them to me.

Turn 5 thinking:

The pattern has held perfectly through two cuts: the light announces the next colour, and the matching wire is cut. Now the light is red and only one wire remains — position 1 under my fingers, the left one. Manual, Deaf's sight, and my touch all converge again: red light, red wire, cut it. There is nothing else on this bomb left to consult and no reason to wait. I make the final clean cut, touch nothing else, and confirm to Deaf by gesture, with the spoken report going to Mute as always.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="The last wire, position one, the red one, is cut — one clean cut, all the way through, nothing else touched. All three wires are now cut and my hands find nothing left to cut on this bomb. Please spell to Deaf that the final cut is done. If the bomb is still live, Deaf should read me whatever the display and light show now, and Mute should check the manual for any rule about a fully cut bomb — I will stand by and touch nothing further until one of them tells me otherwise.")
```
